message.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>
                    Mutations of Odontogenesis-Associated Phosphoprotein (
                    <jats:italic>ODAPH</jats:italic>
                    , OMIM *614829) cause autosomal recessive amelogenesis imperfecta, however, the function of ODAPH during amelogenesis is unknown. Here we characterized normal
                    <jats:italic>Odaph</jats:italic>
                    expression by in situ hybridization, generated
                    <jats:italic>Odaph</jats:italic>
                    truncation mice using CRISPR/Cas9 to replace the TGC codon encoding Cys41 into a TGA translation termination codon, and characterized and compared molar and incisor tooth formation in
                    <jats:italic>Odaph</jats:italic>
                    <jats:sup>+/+</jats:sup>
                    ,
                    <jats:italic>Odaph</jats:italic>
                    <jats:sup>+/C41*</jats:sup>
                    , and
                    <jats:italic>Odaph</jats:italic>
                    <jats:sup>C41*/C41*</jats:sup>
                    mice. We also searched genomes to determine when Odaph first appeared phylogenetically. We determined that tooth development in
                    <jats:italic>Odaph</jats:italic>
                    <jats:sup>+/+</jats:sup>
                    and
                    <jats:italic>Odaph</jats:italic>
                    <jats:sup>+/C41*</jats:sup>
                    mice was indistinguishable in all respects, so the condition in mice is inherited in a recessive pattern, as it is in humans.
                    <jats:italic>Odaph</jats:italic>
                    is specifically expressed by ameloblasts starting with the onset of post-secretory transition and continues until mid-maturation. Based upon histological and ultrastructural analyses, we determined that the secretory stage of amelogenesis is not affected in
                    <jats:italic>Odaph</jats:italic>
                    <jats:sup>C41*/C41*</jats:sup>
                    mice. The enamel layer achieves a normal shape and contour, normal thickness, and normal rod decussation. The fundamental problem in
                    <jats:italic>Odaph</jats:italic>
                    <jats:sup>C41*/C41*</jats:sup>
                    mice starts during post-secretory transition, which fails to generate maturation stage ameloblasts. At the onset of what should be enamel maturation, a cyst forms that separates flattened ameloblasts from the enamel surface. The maturation stage fails completely.
                  </jats:p>
title: Odontogenesis-associated phosphoprotein truncation blocks ameloblast transition into maturation in OdaphC41*/C41* mice
